title: About
text:
This website demonstrates working with Apache Parquet files using PySpark.



Spark Session: Creates a Spark session with the appName “ParquetPenguinsDemo”
Data Loading: Loads the Palmer Penguins dataset
Data Cleaning: Drops all NA values from the dataset
Data Display: Shows the top 10 rows of the cleaned data
Schema Display: Displays the DataFrame schema





Quarto: For creating the static website
PySpark: For data processing
Palmer Penguins: Sample dataset for demonstration
GitHub Actions: For automated deployment




Apache Parquet is a columnar storage file format that is optimized for use with big data processing frameworks. It provides efficient data compression and encoding schemes.

title: Parquet Penguins Demo
text:
This demo shows how to work with the Palmer Penguins dataset using PySpark and Apache Parquet format.

# Import required libraries
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

# Create Spark session with the appName ParquetPenguinsDemo
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("ParquetPenguinsDemo") \
    .master("local[*]") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Load the penguins dataset
penguins_pandas = load_penguins()

# Create a Spark DataFrame from the pandas DataFrame
penguins_df = spark.createDataFrame(penguins_pandas)

# Drop all NA values
penguins_cleaned = penguins_df.dropna()

# Show the top 10 rows
print("Top 10 rows of the cleaned penguins dataset:")
penguins_cleaned.show(10)

# Show the schema
print("\nSchema of the penguins DataFrame:")
penguins_cleaned.printSchema()

# Stop the Spark session
spark.stop()
